titel: Q1: Custom analyzer for case-insensitive Carrier
opdracht:
This set uses the `kibana_sample_data_flights` sample dataset (load it via Kibana > Home > Add sample data).

Define an index `flights_fixed` that includes a custom analyzer called `case-analyzer` for the `Carrier` field, allowing case-insensitive searches. It must use the `standard` tokenizer and a lowercase filter so all characters end up the same case. Reindex the sample data into it and confirm the mapping shows the custom analyzer on `Carrier`.

Topics: Define an index that satisfies requirements; define and use a custom analyzer.
hint: settings.analysis.analyzer.case-analyzer = { type: custom, tokenizer: standard, filter: [lowercase] }. Map Carrier as text with "analyzer": "case-analyzer". Then _reindex from the sample index.

titel: Q2: Dynamic template with Carrier exception
opdracht:
Delete `flights_fixed` and create a new index `kibana_flights` with a dynamic template that maps all string fields as keyword, EXCEPT the `Carrier` field, which should be text with a lowercase (custom) analyzer. Reindex the sample data into `kibana_flights` and check the mappings.

Topics: Define and use a dynamic template.

Note: this exercise assumes `flights_fixed` exists from Q1 so it can be deleted first.
hint: dynamic_templates with match_mapping_type "string", match "*", unmatch "Carrier" -> keyword. Explicitly map Carrier as text + case-analyzer. Then _reindex.

setup.naam: Ensure flights_fixed exists (so it can be deleted)

titel: Q3: ILM policy for time-series flights
opdracht:
Define an ILM policy `flights_ILM` with these phases:
- Hot: roll over after 5 minutes.
- Warm: 3 minutes after rollover, forcemerge to 1 segment, shrink to 1 shard.
- Cold: 6 minutes after rollover, set replicas to 0.
- Delete: 8 minutes after rollover.

Topics: Define an ILM policy for a time-series index.
hint: hot.actions.rollover.max_age 5m. warm.min_age 8m with forcemerge + shrink. cold.min_age 11m with allocate replicas 0. delete.min_age 13m. (min_age counts from rollover.)

titel: Q4: Boolean query for delayed/cancelled US flights
opdracht:
Retrieve flights that were either delayed by >= 60 minutes OR canceled, where the destination country was `US`. Show only `DestCountry`, `Cancelled`, `FlightDelayMin`. Add a terms aggregation counting how many of those US flights had `Cancelled` true vs false.

Topics: Boolean combination of queries and filters; bucket aggregation.

Run this against the `kibana_sample_data_flights` index.
hint: bool.should [ range FlightDelayMin gte 60, term Cancelled true ] + minimum_should_match 1, bool.filter [ term DestCountry US ]. _source the 3 fields. aggs terms on Cancelled.

titel: Q5: Cross-cluster search with avg price
opdracht:
Implement a search that retrieves flights across TWO clusters, filtering for flights originating from "Tokyo Haneda International Airport" and calculating the average ticket price.

Topics: Query across multiple clusters; metric aggregation.

This exercise needs a second cluster, so there is no automatic check - write and run it against your own multi-cluster setup. The model answer shows the remote registration and the CCS query.
hint: Register the remote via PUT _cluster/settings (cluster.remote.<name>.seeds). Then query both indices: GET local,remote:index/_search with a term on Origin and an avg agg on AvgTicketPrice.

titel: Q6: Runtime field for flight time in hours
opdracht:
Write a search on `kibana_sample_data_flights` that uses a runtime field to calculate total flight time in HOURS (FlightTimeMin / 60) and filters for flights longer than 10 hours. Also expose the same value via a scripted field. Show `FlightNum` and the runtime field.

Topics: Search that utilizes a runtime field.
hint: runtime_mappings.total_flight_time (double) emit(doc['FlightTimeMin'].value / 60.0). Filter range gte 10. script_fields for the scripted version.

opdracht:
Write a query that searches for flights with "Weather Delay" in the `FlightDelayType` field and highlights the matched term in the results.

Topics: Highlight the search terms in the response of a query.
hint: Use a match query on FlightDelayType, then a highlight block: { fields: { FlightDelayType: {} } }. (FlightDelayType is a keyword; use match or term.)

opdracht:
Define an ingest pipeline `flightstatus_pipeline` that adds a field `Flight Status` based on `FlightDelay` and `Cancelled` using Painless:
- delayed -> "Delayed"
- canceled -> "Cancelled"
- otherwise -> "On time".
Then remove the `FlightDelay` and `Cancelled` fields. Reindex the sample data into `flights_with_status` using this pipeline.

Topics: Ingest pipeline with Painless to modify documents.
hint: script processor building a String from ctx.FlightDelay / ctx.Cancelled, assign ctx['Flight Status']. Then a remove processor for the two fields. Reindex with dest.pipeline.

opdracht:
Delete `kibana_sample_data_flights` locally and set up cross-cluster replication for it from your `cluster2_remote`, creating a follower index named `flights_replicated`. Also ensure the data is backed up via a snapshot repository.

Topics: Cross-cluster replication; snapshot backup.

This exercise needs a second cluster and a registered snapshot repository, so there is no automatic check - use your own multi-cluster setup. The model answer shows the full flow.
hint: Register a snapshot repo (Stack Management > Snapshot and Restore), take a snapshot, DELETE the local index, then PUT /flights_replicated/_ccr/follow with remote_cluster + leader_index.
modelantwoord:
PUT _snapshot/flights_repo/my-snap
{ "indices": "kibana_sample_data_flights" }

DELETE kibana_sample_data_flights

PUT /flights_replicated/_ccr/follow
{
  "remote_cluster": "cluster2_remote",
  "leader_index": "kibana_sample_data_flights",
  "max_read_request_operation_count": 5120,
  "max_outstanding_read_requests": 12,
  "max_read_request_size": "32mb",
  "read_poll_timeout": "1m"
}

GET flights_replicated/_search

opdracht:
Create a search template `day_of_week_search` (mustache) that queries flights on a specific `dayOfWeek` and supports pagination via `from` and `size` params. Then run it with query_number = 2, the third page, 10 docs per page.

Topics: Pagination; search templates.

Note: third page at 10 per page means from = 20. Test data is staged in `flights_tpl_test` so the template call has an index to run against.
hint: PUT _scripts/day_of_week_search with lang mustache: query match dayOfWeek {{query_number}}, from {{from}}, size {{size}}. Call via _search/template with params from=20, size=10.
